text:
maria: Heads up — hitting a weird hang on Windows in the Python SDK when connections are being recycled during a burst. Repro in our CI Windows runners, but not on Linux.

ken: Seen anything in logs? stack traces?

maria: No traceback, just the test process stuck. Threads all show asyncio tasks waiting in connector acquire/release. Minimal repro below.

ravi: can you paste the snippet? maybe related to uvloop/asyncio mismatch on Windows.

maria: Sure — gist (inline):
```python
import asyncio
import httpx

async def worker(i):
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5.0, limits=httpx.Limits(max_connections=10)) as c:
        for _ in range(50):
            await c.get('http://127.0.0.1:8000/')

async def main():
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(worker(i)) for i in range(40)]
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

asyncio.run(main())
```

maria: On Windows, after ~30s it just hangs when the server replies with a Connection: keep-alive and we force a small recycle window on the server.

lucy: is uwloop installed on Windows CI? uvloop doesn't support Windows — that might explain differences.

maria: Right, CI uses asyncio on Windows, uvloop on Linux. But we still see a hang even with asyncio only when the client does aggressive churn and server closes sockets mid-exchange.

ken: Could be a race in httpx/urllib3 connector closing sockets while they're being returned to the pool. Any leak in selectors or pending tasks?

ravi: I dug into httpx TCPConnector code — there is a connection_reuse path that uses weakrefs. If finalize happens during release it can drop into a waiting acquire. Might be semaphore starvation.

nate: I've seen similar with a custom semaphore we used for per-host concurrency — when the connection is forcibly closed, release() sometimes doesn't run, leaving the semaphore count off by one => starvation under high concurrency.

maria: We reproduced with a stripped-down server that calls conn.shutdown(SHUT_RDWR) and then close after a tiny delay. Linux still fine. Windows sockets sometimes linger in TIME_WAIT in a way that confuses our release hooks.

lucy: Any workaround for now? lower concurrency?

maria: Lowering client parallelism avoids it. Also switching to httpx with limits and explicit pool_recycle on server side helps. But need a fix.

ken: Can you try forcing explicit close in finally block before returning the connection to pool? e.g. call await resp.aclose() and ensure transport is closed.

maria: Tried that; reduces frequency but doesn't eliminate. Also tried python 3.11 vs 3.12 — same.

ravi: Filing a minimal issue with reproduction will help. Also, we should add a unit test that runs on Windows runners with short timeouts so CI will catch regressions.

maria: I opened a draft PR with the repro harness + failing test: https://stash/.../pr/42 (internal).

deploy-bot: CI pipeline triggered for PR #42 — windows-runners/20 queued :gear:

lucy: Long-term, we should expose a small, explicit connection lifecycle API in the SDK: a context manager that separates "borrow" vs "ensure_closed" semantics. Right now AsyncClient hides too much. Typing would help here too — explicit protocols for Connection objects.

nate: +1 on typing. I've been bitten by unclear types for limits and pool config. Feature request: add max_inflight_per_origin and a recycle_timeout option on AsyncClient.limits with typed NamedTuple or dataclass so mypy can catch misuse.

ken: Could be a breaking change; propose adding new param name 'concurrency_limits' as a dataclass to avoid overloading Limits constructor. Keep old API backward compatible but warn.

maria: Also propose a small sample app under devex samples showing correct shutdown: startup creates AsyncClient singleton, on SIGTERM run client.aclose() before loop stop. Many customers get burned by lifecycle anti-patterns in tutorials.

ravi: I'll sketch a PR: 1) add reproducible test for Windows 2) add optional 'concurrency_limits' dataclass, 3) add improved typing stubs for AsyncClient and Connection objects, 4) add sample shutdown snippet to docs.

lucy: We should also add a short item to the SDK changelog about Windows semantics — network stack differences are real.

maria: For immediate unblock, can someone run my PR on Windows runners and paste logs? seems flakey so need multiple runs.

nate: running now on my fork; will post results.

nate: First run hung at 1825001248, second run passed, third run hung. Logs show tasks waiting at httpx._backends.httpcore.AsyncHTTPTransport.request acquire.

ravi: That points to httpcore. We might need a guard that catches CancelledError during release and still calls semaphore.release(). I'll open an upstream issue on httpx/httpcore.

maria: Thanks — please @mention me in the upstream issue. If upstream fix takes long, we'll add an SDK-level workaround.

ken: For the workaround, implement a robust release wrapper with try/except/finally that ensures semaphore consistency. Add unit that forcibly cancels tasks during release to validate.

lucy: Small doc request: include recommended patterns for AsyncClient in sample apps (singleton vs transient clients) and emphasize explicit close in signal handlers. That'll reduce customer tickets.

maria: Agreed — I'll push a docs patch and a sample repo. Also adding a typed example for the new concurrency dataclass.

deploy-bot: PR #42 windows-run: completed with 2/5 flakes :warning:

maria: Good enough to move forward. Thanks all. Will link PRs and upstream issues in #devex when available. :raised_hands:
